chunks: And from al-'Idah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Ziyad ibn Abi Raja, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Say what you know, and if you do not know then say: 'Allah is more knowing.' Indeed, a man may pick out a verse from the Qur'an and fall into it (misinterpret it) a distance farther than what is between the sky and the earth.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of picking a single verse from the Quran without context?
ai.summary: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) instructs believers to speak only with knowledge and to say 'Allah is more knowing' when uncertain. He warns that selectively extracting a verse from the Qur'an without full context leads to significant error in interpretation.

en.ammaar-muslim: 3. [3/37] al-Kafi: And from a number from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from al-Hasan b. Ali al-Washsha from Aban al-Ahmar from Ziyad b. Abi Raja from Abi Ja’far عليه السلام who said:

say what you know and if you do not know then say: “Allāh is more knowing”, a man selectively picks out a verse from the Qur’an and falls in it (misinterpreting it) a farther distance than what is between the earth and the sky.
